title: First after Op Sindoor: India invites Pak to SCO meeting in Delhi

practice.q: Despite frozen bilateral ties, India continues to engage Pakistan through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). Discuss the significance of such multilateral engagement for India.
parts: Introduction: tensions with Pakistan, yet engagement through the SCO
India's engagement with Pakistan at the SCO (multi-dimensional)
Significance of multilateral engagement for India: positives (multi-dimensional)
Way forward with conclusion (10 marks, so combined)

answer.t: India–Pakistan bilateral relations have remained frozen for a decade over Pakistan's state policy of cross-border terrorism, from the Pathankot and Uri attacks (2016) to the Pahalgam attack and Operation Sindoor (2025). Yet India continues to engage Pakistan on multilateral platforms, most recently by inviting Pakistan's culture minister to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi (20–21 November 2026).

answer.h: India's engagement with Pakistan at the SCO

pts.t: As host of an SCO event, India must invite every member state; engagement here is a matter of institutional rules, not a bilateral concession.
pts.ex: India's invitation to Pakistan's culture minister for the Civilisational Dialogue Forum, 2026.

pts.t: The SCO has kept ministerial contact alive even when bilateral visits stopped, avoiding a complete diplomatic breakdown.
pts.ex: Bilawal Bhutto attended the SCO Foreign Ministers' meeting in Goa (2023); EAM Jaishankar went to Islamabad for the SCO Heads of Government meeting (2024).

pts.t: India uses the SCO to push connectivity, which Pakistan's position between India and Central Asia makes central to any regional plan.
pts.ex: An Indian Additional Secretary flagged 'connectivity, regional connectivity, transit and trade' at the SCO national coordinators' meeting in Islamabad (2026).

pts.t: Overland transit through Pakistan is India's shortest route to Afghanistan and Central Asia; the SCO is the only forum where both sit at the same table on it.
pts.ex: Transit was among the issues India raised in Islamabad (2026).

pts.t: With bilateral trade largely suspended, the SCO keeps the idea of regional economic cooperation alive.
pts.ex: 'Trade' was part of the agenda India flagged at the SCO coordinators' meeting (2026).

pts.t: A soft, low-risk track that rests on shared heritage rather than disputed politics.
pts.ex: The Civilisational Dialogue Forum, proposed by PM Modi at the Tianjin summit (2025), on shared Eurasian heritage, art and literature.

answer.h: Significance of multilateral engagement for India

pts.k: Strategic posture: bilateral freeze, multilateral engagement
pts.t: India keeps up pressure on Pakistan over terror while avoiding the appearance of isolating itself or blocking regional cooperation.
pts.ex: Inviting Pakistan to Delhi while bilateral ties stay frozen.

pts.t: The SCO's counter-terrorism framework gives India a platform to raise cross-border terrorism before Pakistan and its partners.
pts.ex: The SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) as a venue to press India's concerns.

pts.t: The SCO links India to energy-rich, landlocked Central Asian markets that matter for its trade and energy security.
pts.ex: Connectivity and transit raised alongside Central Asian members such as Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

pts.t: Civilisational diplomacy projects India's cultural leadership and builds goodwill beyond governments.
pts.ex: The Civilisational Dialogue is expected to be held at one of Delhi's iconic monuments.

pts.t: Membership keeps India inside a grouping of Russia, China and Central Asia, balancing its ties with the West.
pts.ex: India's SCO coordinator described the SCO as a journey where 'Eurasian and Asian landmass member states have come together'.

pts.t: Proposing and hosting new initiatives lets India shape the grouping instead of reacting to it.
pts.ex: PM Modi's Tianjin (2025) proposal became an SCO forum hosted by India in 2026.

pts.t: Multilateral courtesy cannot substitute for an end to terror; every attack resets ties.
pts.ex: The Pahalgam attack (2025) followed years of engagement attempts.

pts.t: China's closeness to Pakistan can dilute SCO positions that India wants on terror and connectivity.
pts.ex: India's opposition to the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor, which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

pts.t: Decisions need every member's agreement, so outcomes are often declaratory rather than binding.
pts.ex: India declined to endorse the SCO Defence Ministers' joint statement in June 2025 because it left out the Pahalgam attack.

answer.t: India should use the SCO to keep raising terrorism through RATS, advance connectivity and culture where interests converge, and link any bilateral step to verifiable action by Pakistan against terror. Multilateral engagement thus lets India remain firm on security while staying diplomatically present in Eurasia, a pragmatic balance between principle and interest.
